tip: çektirdim adds -tir- to çekmek so it means I had it pulled, not I pulled. The doer takes the dative, here Dişçiye (by the dentist).
Adding -ınca to a verb means once or when it happens. açınca is once it opened, said of the sun coming out.
Turkish builds fractions backwards. üçte bir is literally in three, one, which means one third.
To say under something, the object takes genitive and alt takes a location ending. yatağın altında is under the bed.
To turn a whole action into a noun, the doer takes genitive and the verb takes -ması. Dedemin kapatması is my grandfather's closing.
için after a plain -mak verb means in order to. kutlamak için is in order to celebrate.
To say because, put -dığı için on the verb. uyuyamadığım için is because I could not sleep.
The suffix -ce on a group means all together as that group. ailece is as a whole family.
For an unreal past, use -mış olsaydı in the if part. yatmış olsaydım is if I had gone to bed.
-mıştım marks an action already finished before another past moment. çıkmıştım is I had already left.
konuşulur adds the passive -ul- to konuşmak, so it means are spoken with no named speaker.
Put en before an adjective to make the most. en çalışkan is the most hardworking.
-en turns a verb into an adjective sitting before its noun. ekilen buğday is the wheat that was planted.
Add -ıncı to a number to make the ordinal. altı becomes Altıncı, the sixth.
göre after a dative noun means compared to, and daha marks the comparison. şehre göre daha temiz is cleaner than the city.
When a verb is the object of another verb it takes -meyi. gitmeyi planlıyoruz is we are planning to go.
gidemeyeceğim stacks -eme, meaning cannot, onto the future, so it is I will not be able to go.
